subject: health
unitTitle: Safety, Injury Prevention, and Digital Life
title: Application or project: basic first aid and when to get an adult
focus: basic first aid and when to get an adult
essentialQuestion: How do I prevent harm and respond well when something goes wrong?
materials: paper and pencil or an accessible response tool
the fictional lesson cards included in this task
keyPoints: Small cut: wash with clean water, apply gentle pressure, cover.
Burn: cool under running water for around 20 minutes, then get an adult.
Never use ice, butter, or cream.
Nosebleed: sit up, lean forward, pinch the soft part of the nose.
Always get an adult for head injuries, bleeding that will not stop, breathing trouble, a suspected broken bone, or any loss of consciousness.
Your job is to recognise and fetch help, not to treat someone yourself.
privacySafeScenario: All required evidence uses fictional or public situations. The learner never has to disclose personal health, body, treatment, feelings, family, sexual, or substance-use information.
studentTask: Write two facts. Use the lesson idea about basic first aid and when to get an adult. Choose one safe next step. Name an adult or help source.
knowledgeCheck: Name the fact. Fix the wrong claim. Choose a safe action. Name who can help.
completionCriteria: I explain basic first aid and when to get an adult.
I choose a safe action and give a reason.
I name the right kind of help.
adaptationChoices: Show one short direction at a time. Allow reading aloud, word cards, typing, writing, drawing with labels, signing, selecting, or speaking. Help may repeat a direction but may not choose the fact, action, reason, or help source.
extensionChallenge: Create a new fictional or public case about basic first aid and when to get an adult. Include enough facts, choices or constraints, and support authority for another learner to reason safely. Add an accurate explanation of acceptable variation; use no real person's private information.
accessibilitySupports: Show one action at a time.
Offer a vocabulary card and extra time.
Accept typing, writing, drawing with labels, signing, selecting, or speaking for equal credit.
trustedAdultNote: If a real situation feels unsafe or raises a health concern, pause the lesson and tell a parent, guardian, teacher, school staff member, or another trusted adult. A qualified health professional gives medical advice. In an emergency, get an adult and use the local emergency service.

optionalReflection.prompt: Optional and private: Make up one example that helps you remember basic first aid and when to get an adult. Keep it for yourself. You do not need to show it or prove that you completed it.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, body-fat percentage, body comparison, or appearance scoring.
This task never requires calorie counting, dieting, or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires sharing medical history, a diagnosis, treatment, medication, feelings, family conflict, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
This task never requires advice about an individual learner's treatment, medication, food, supplement, or exercise plan.

remediation.alternateExplanation: Use a bridge diagram: NEED and EVIDENCE are one side; ACTION, AUTHORITY, SAFEGUARD, and MEASURE are the spans. A proposal cannot cross the bridge when one span is missing.
